# Authoring contract

The private Task Source integration uses POST /internal/v1/source-authoring-jobs with the strict tz-source-authoring-request.v1 envelope and a nested prepared-source-task.v1. This entrypoint validates exact GitHub commit/path provenance and content digest, then maps the typed source content into the same private planning job and existing generation, canonical target resolution, verification, persistence, and READY-only technical-task.v1 projection. It does not publish to Practice. Existing manifest request schemas v1/v2 and their routes remain unchanged.

## Input

`tz-planning-request.v1` is a strict object with:

- `mode`: `private` or `canonical`;
- `manifest`: required, trimmed, at most 64 KiB;
- `locale`: `ru` or `en`;
- `source`: exact source type plus optional HTTPS provenance;
- `classification_hints`: optional task type and bounded stack codes.

`tz-planning-request.v1` remains byte/hash compatible and has no
`orchestration` field; its trusted `surface_classification` is always
`practice`. `tz-planning-request.v2` has the same fields and requires this
additional strict object:

```json
{
  "orchestration": {
    "schema": "learning-workspace-authoring-intent.v1",
    "trigger": "planner_recommendation | student_project",
    "correlation_id": "UUID",
    "surface_classification": "practice | project",
    "desired_difficulty_level": "beginner | junior | junior_plus | middle | senior"
  }
}
```

`desired_difficulty_level` is optional; the other orchestration fields are
required. The intent deliberately has no student/profile/mastery/path/dialog
data or URL. A caller derives this bounded authoring intent from owner data;
TZ Planner never reads Student state.

Common input aliases (`js`, `ecmascript`, `golang`, `html5`, `css3`) are
normalized to canonical stack codes before target discovery; they never become
competency aliases.

Creation requires a UUID `Idempotency-Key`. The key is bound to the SHA-256 of
the normalized request, including the complete v2 orchestration intent. Reusing
it with another request is a conflict; exact replay returns the stored job.

`READY` and `STAGED` are terminal authoring results for exact create and resume
replay. After request normalization and the existing dependency configuration
checks, replay returns the unchanged stored job before fresh generation or an
attempt-cap rejection, including a job staged on its fifth authoring attempt.
Artifact, private staging receipt, attempts, lease and owner timestamps remain
unchanged. Configured downstream ports are not invoked. A different normalized
request still conflicts; nonterminal lease, attempt-cap and failed-retry behavior
remain unchanged. This does not change Stage behavior or the existing
READY-only TechnicalTask read availability. `STAGED` remains private Practice
acceptance, separate from Practice-owned approval and public publication.

The gated T22.2 `TestT222ActualStagedReplay` proof composes production Planner
and PostgreSQL lifecycle with named generator, competency, runtime-profile,
validation, workspace and staging collaborators. Root seeds actual Plan+Stage
rows, including an attempt-five job reached through four Claim+SaveFailed
cycles, then starts a separate Go test process that replays the exact stored
requests and keys. Trap counters and retained row/xmin, artifact, receipt,
attempts, lease and timestamp checks distinguish replay from new work.
This proves the TZ owner replay contract rather than actual model generation,
validator execution, Practice service acceptance or public release.

Root alone runs the declared seed/replay commands with `T222_TZ_PROOF=1`,
`T222_TZ_PHASE=seed|replay`, and
`T222_TZ_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:58998/remediation_t222_tz_integration_proof?sslmode=disable`.
Required `T222_TZ_SEED_FILE` and optional `T222_TZ_RESULT_FILE` belong in the
owned T22 evidence directory. Root provisions only this new disposable
database using existing migrations 001/002/003 through the ledger. The commands
do not migrate, reset, delete retained rows, start services or execute sources;
the test skips without its explicit proof gate.

## Public blueprint

`practice-task-blueprint.v1` contains:

- stable `family_key` and meaningful `variant_key`;
- authored `surface_classification` (`practice` or `project`), task type,
  domain, stack, topology, and six independent difficulty axes;
- scenario with at least one role, requirements, constraints, non-goals, and
  acceptance criteria;
- milestone DAG with first-class Step DAGs, deliverables, effort, acceptance,
  exact learning requirements, validator mappings, and optional assistance
  override;
- exact runtime-profile `(code, version, digest)` and starter workspace;
- validator v1, review policy v2, AssistancePolicy v1, complete traceability,
  source provenance, and generation provenance.

The local typed quality gate rejects unknown JSON fields, unsupported enums,
invalid IDs/paths/digests, cycles, dangling references, uncovered acceptance
criteria, unverified requirements, unresolved learning requirements, incomplete
traceability, and any policy permitting the Teacher to write a complete
solution. Text and identifier fields are normalized before digest calculation
using the same staging-boundary digest rules as Practice, so a `READY` candidate is
digest-stable across that boundary.

`candidate_digest` hashes the complete candidate, including private evaluation,
after canonical JSON normalization. Object-key order and whitespace inside
embedded raw JSON therefore remain stable after PostgreSQL `jsonb` persistence
and when Practice checks the staging request.

The same normalized candidate is projected into `technical-task.v1` without an
additional model call. The TechnicalTask read contract explicitly separates
`goal`, `student_instruction`, `expected_result`, `concepts`, `steps`, and
`verification`; its full schema and invariants are documented in
[TechnicalTask contract](technical-task-contract.md).
The unchanged `technical-task.v1` schema has no surface field; its build gate
validates the exact surface on the single persisted Blueprint source rather
than duplicating the Practice-owned classification fact.

Learning policies are `required`, `recommended`, `optional`, or `adaptive`.
They point only to exact canonical `(type, key, version)` targets; titles and
generated prose never identify a competency.

## Private authoring bundle

`tz-authoring-candidate.v1` wraps the public blueprint and a private evaluation
bundle containing the executable `code_structure`, one passing reference
fixture, and 1–20 failing negative fixtures. This bundle is durable for audit
and retry but is never projected by the HTTP API or published as student
content.

TZ Planner overwrites source hash, job identity, prompt/policy identity, tone,
methodology, skill references, and `surface_classification` with trusted
server-side values before its quality gate. Model-supplied provenance or
surface is never authoritative. When v2 supplies desired difficulty, the
generated `difficulty.derived_level` must match it exactly; TZ does not invent
or modify the six authored axes.

`source.educational_adaptation` is the preferred student-facing task
description. For backward-compatible candidates where it is absent, the
TechnicalTask projection derives the description from the first public
requirement and never exposes the internal scenario goal as student prose.

## Fixed authoring method

Policy `task-authoring-v1` uses tone `supportive_direct`, methodology
`incremental_evidence_first`, and these versioned skill references:

- `task_analysis.v1`;
- `meaningful_variant_design.v1`;
- `step_decomposition.v1`;
- `competency_mapping.v1`;
- `evaluation_design.v1`;
- `traceability_audit.v1`.

These are generation-policy identifiers and deterministic responsibilities,
not autonomous production agents. The fixed prompt is
`practice-task.authoring-candidate.v1@2`. It receives a bounded canonical
target vocabulary discovered from Learning Planner; every selected identity is
still exact-resolved after generation. Its server-owned authoring policy also
declares the `technical-task.v1` field boundaries and deterministic mapping, so
one coherent candidate response supplies the complete task. Projection,
sorting, normalization, and student DTO creation are ordinary code paths and do
not consume tokens. For v2 the prompt also receives only the bounded
`learning-workspace-authoring-intent.v1` object; server enforcement remains
authoritative.
